# Privacy notice

This notice explains how the mobility-model-zoo processes personal data when it collects texts, labels them and trains and publishes models. It is the information required by Art. 14 GDPR for data that was not collected from you directly. Last updated: 2026-10-08.

## Who is responsible

Martin Habedank (private person) runs the mobility-model-zoo privately and is the controller.

- Privacy requests: privacy@miskatonic-analytics.com
- Other questions: contact@miskatonic-analytics.com
- Imprint: https://miskatonic-analytics.com/imprint.html
- Privacy policy of the website behind these addresses: https://miskatonic-analytics.com/privacy.html

The project is non-commercial: it sells nothing, takes no payments and runs no advertising.

## What we do and why

We build small machine learning models for mobility and publish them openly. For one task (extracting jobs-to-be-done, pains and gains from texts) we collect published texts, remove personal identifiers, have language models label them, and use the labeled texts to build a benchmark and to train models. We publish the models, their documentation and evaluation numbers. **We never publish the collected texts or the labels.**

Personal data appears in these texts only incidentally: names of people who speak in public parliamentary sessions, statements of research interview participants as published by the researchers, and posts in public forums. We do not build profiles of people, and the models do not store or return the texts they were trained on: they mark passages in the text a user gives them.

## Sources and legal basis

### machine-sound-datasets

Published recordings of machine sounds (fans, pumps, valves, slide rails) from research datasets, downloaded from the publishers.
Used for: not used yet.

- Legal basis: no personal data is processed.
- Special categories: none expected; the data are sensor recordings without free text, and they are never sent to a language model.
- Safeguards: Licence and use check per dataset, data kept outside git with a retention date, no publication of the data.
- Retention: Local cache only; delete 12 months after the last training run that used it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

### imu-activity-datasets

Published motion-sensor recordings of volunteers (accelerometer and gyroscope windows, subjects identified only by number) from research datasets, downloaded from the publishers.
Used for: not used yet.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Train and evaluate activity recognition on microcontrollers. Why it does not override your interests: Volunteers took part in a published study; the publishers identify subjects only by number; the data is not redistributed and the model outputs only an activity class.
- Special categories: none expected; the data are sensor recordings without free text, and they are never sent to a language model.
- Safeguards: Licence and use check per dataset, data kept outside git with a retention date, no publication of the data, no attempt to re-identify subjects, objection channel (PRIVACY.md).
- Retention: Local cache only; delete 12 months after the last training run that used it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

### Parliamentary records

Plenary and committee records published by parliaments (Germany, UK, Ireland, US, Wales, Scotland, EU, Austria, Switzerland, German state parliaments, Canada).
Used for: training (43 sources) and the evaluation benchmark only (29 sources).
Publishers: UK Parliament; Houses of the Oireachtas; Deutscher Bundestag; Abgeordnetenhaus Berlin; Senedd Cymru; Schweizer Parlament; Bayerischer Landtag; European Parliament; U.S. Government Publishing Office; Niedersächsischer Landtag; House of Commons of Canada; Österreichisches Parlament; The Scottish Parliament.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Build and evaluate a model that extracts jobs, pains and gains from mobility debates. Why it does not override your interests: Speakers are office holders or invited witnesses speaking in a public, recorded setting intended for publication; texts are not redistributed; the model outputs only spans of the user's own input, never stored records.
- Special categories: Political opinions expressed by office holders in parliamentary records are not quarantined (Art. 9(2)(e) GDPR); health, religion and other special categories about third persons in those records are still flagged.
- Safeguards: Redaction of contact identifiers, texts kept outside git with a retention date, no publication of training text, objection channel (PRIVACY.md), suppression list.
- Retention: Review 24 months after the dataset freeze; delete when no current model needs it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

### Research interviews

Interview transcripts from research datasets published on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0.
Used for: training (42 sources).
Publishers: Zenodo (CERN).

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Build and evaluate a model that extracts jobs, pains and gains from interviews. Why it does not override your interests: Datasets were published by researchers for reuse, pseudonymised by the publishers; consent basis is recorded per dataset or flagged for an owner decision.
- Special categories (health, religion, political opinions and the other categories of Art. 9 GDPR) are detected and excluded before labeling.
- Safeguards: Redaction, no redistribution, retention date, objection channel, suppression list.
- Retention: Review 24 months after the dataset freeze; delete when no current model needs it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

### Openly licensed papers

Scientific papers and reports under open licences (CC BY 4.0) used for training.
Used for: training (2 sources).
Publishers: Elsevier BV; Springer Science and Business Media LLC.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Build and evaluate a model that extracts jobs, pains and gains from research texts. Why it does not override your interests: Published for reuse under an open licence; the people quoted in papers are mostly anonymised study participants.
- Special categories (health, religion, political opinions and the other categories of Art. 9 GDPR) are detected and excluded before labeling.
- Safeguards: Redaction, no redistribution, retention date, attribution in the model card.
- Retention: Review 24 months after the dataset freeze; delete when no current model needs it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

### Documents used under the text and data mining exception

Papers, reports and transcripts without an open licence, used only in the benchmark under the text and data mining exception (§44b UrhG).
Used for: the evaluation benchmark only (23 sources).
Publishers: Springer Science and Business Media LLC; Elsevier BV; Informa UK Limited; University of Westminster Press; MDPI AG; Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR); Agora Verkehrswende; Hans-Böckler-Stiftung; Bundeszentrale für politische Bildung; Europe PMC (EMBL-EBI); infas / BMDV (Mobilität in Deutschland); Öko-Institut; Stiftung Mercator.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Evaluate extraction quality on realistic, varied texts. Why it does not override your interests: Used only for evaluation, never for training or redistribution; opt-outs honoured.
- Special categories (health, religion, political opinions and the other categories of Art. 9 GDPR) are detected and excluded before labeling.
- Safeguards: benchmark_only, retention date, no publication of text, deletion when not needed.
- Retention: Delete when the benchmark is retired; review 24 months after freeze. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark.

### Public forum posts

Public forum posts about mobility, used only in the benchmark (§44b UrhG).
Used for: the evaluation benchmark only (39 sources).
Forums: beteiligungsportal.baden-wuerttemberg.de, brummionline.com, drehscheibe-online.de, forum-speditionen.de, forum.cyclinguk.org, goingelectric.de, ice-treff.de, lemmy.ca, motor-talk.de, stummiforum.de.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Evaluate extraction quality on informal user texts, where real pains are stated. Why it does not override your interests: Posts are public but written by private persons; usernames and contact identifiers are redacted before labeling; texts are never used for training or published.
- Special categories (health, religion, political opinions and the other categories of Art. 9 GDPR) are detected and excluded before labeling.
- Safeguards: benchmark_only, redaction plus local model review, special categories quarantined, platform terms checked (C-I7), objection channel and suppression list.
- Retention: Delete when the benchmark is retired; review 24 months after freeze. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark.

### can-bus-datasets

Published CAN bus and vehicle-network recordings from research datasets (frame logs of test vehicles, simulated V2X messages, GNSS receiver features), downloaded from the publishers.
Used for: not used yet.

- Legal basis: legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. Our interest: Train and evaluate intrusion and spoofing detectors for vehicle networks. Why it does not override your interests: Recordings come from research test vehicles and simulations published for reuse; they may contain vehicle identifiers or positions of the test vehicles, not of private drivers; the data is not redistributed and models output only alarm scores.
- Special categories: none expected; the data are sensor recordings without free text, and they are never sent to a language model.
- Safeguards: Licence and use check per dataset, data kept outside git in a local cache with a retention date, no publication of the data, objection channel (PRIVACY.md).
- Retention: Local cache only; delete 12 months after the last training run that used it. Purpose: Reproduce the frozen benchmark and the training set of a current model.

## Recipients

The texts are labeled by language models. Labeling runs on the controller's own computer where possible. The following routes received texts; the list is generated from the labeling logs.

| Route | Who received the texts | Region | Retention by the recipient | Used for | Period | Calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-consumer-cli` | Anthropic (consumer plan via Claude Code CLI; contracting entity for EEA users Anthropic Ireland, Limited) | IE (contracting entity) / US (processing) | stored for a limited time (see the provider's terms) | reference | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06 | 331 |
| `gpt-mini-openrouter-openai` | OpenAI (via OpenRouter, Inc., US) | US | stored for a limited time (see the provider's terms) | reference | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06 | 330 |
| `local-spark-ollama` | local:spark | DE (owner's machine) | not stored | baseline, teacher_candidate | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-07 | 899 |
| `mimo-openrouter-deepinfra` | DeepInfra (Deep Infra Inc., US; via OpenRouter, Inc., US) | US | not stored | teacher, teacher_candidate | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-07 | 1250 |
| `mimo-openrouter-unrecorded` | unknown (failed attempts; OpenRouter did not report a provider) | unknown | unknown | teacher, teacher_candidate | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06 | 7392 |
| `wafer-openrouter` | Wafer (Wafer, Inc., US; via OpenRouter, Inc., US) | US | unknown | teacher_candidate | 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-06 | 596 |

Calls include failed attempts, in which the text was sent but no answer was used. OpenRouter, Inc. (US) forwards requests to the hosting provider; it does not store prompts or responses by default.

Recipients in the United States are not listed under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework; transfers rely on the providers' standard contractual clauses where they offer them. New labeling with hosted models only runs through routes that the controller has approved in `compliance/providers.yaml`. The models are published on Hugging Face and the code on GitHub; they contain no collected texts.

## Your rights

You have the right to access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18) and data portability (Art. 20). Write to privacy@miskatonic-analytics.com with a link or a short description of the text that concerns you. We answer within one month.

## Your right to object (Art. 21 GDPR)

**You can object at any time, for reasons arising from your particular situation, to the processing of personal data about you that is based on our legitimate interest.** Write to privacy@miskatonic-analytics.com. We then stop processing the text in question, delete it from our collections and add it to a suppression list, so that it is not collected again and not used for future training, unless we can show compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests.

Please do not post personal details in public GitHub issues. The issue template "Rights request" is only for requests that contain no personal data, such as opt-outs of whole websites.

## Complaints

You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example Berliner Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit.

## How we handle requests

See [docs/compliance/requests.md](https://github.com/mhabedank/mobility-model-zoo/blob/main/docs/compliance/requests.md). Request records hold no names, only a keyed hash.
